provider: NIRD Data Lake (Sigma2, Norway) — S3 object storage, 10 TB single-object support, 100M objects/bucket

free_tier.stated: No fixed per-project byte number published. Quota is set per project by the Resource Allocation Committee (RFK) in TiB on NIRD Data Peak and/or Data Lake separately. What IS fixed and unusually generous: 'NIRD S3 supports 10TB single object sizes and up to 100 million objects per bucket', total NIRD capacity 75 PB (24 PB DP + 51 PB DL), and measured throughput '27GB/s'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Unmetered; S3 and HTTPS serve directly, and NIRD S3 is explicitly for 'data sharing with external collaborators' and 'data streaming'.

tooling: Rclone (provider = Other, endpoint https://s3.nird.sigma2.no), AWS CLI, s3cmd, MinIO client, Cyberduck. The same data is simultaneously available over POSIX, NFS and S3. 'the same data can be accessed simultaneously through multiple protocols'.
chaining: Quota is per project and RFK-allocated, so the multiplier is project count and the DP/DL split (two resources, 'The two resources have separate quota based on the project allocation'). NIRD Data Lake is pitched at 'structured or unstructured data of any volume larger than 1 TiB'. I.e. the intended workload IS tens of TB.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: 10 TB per single object, 100M objects per bucket. The most permissive object caps in this niche. Retention: 'long-term storage of non-persistent data'; Data Lake has NO on-demand backup ('On-demand backup | Yes | No'), only erasure coding and snapshots. request-rate: not published (27 GB/s aggregate is the claim). Gate: Norwegian university/research affiliation plus RFK allocation.

identity_cost.detail: Applicants belong to a listed Norwegian organisation (universities and university colleges, governmental research centres, hospitals, industrial parties); the project leader holds a permanent, postdoctoral or temporary position; master and PhD students and guest researchers apply through a colleague.

reliability_note: CRITICAL COST CAVEAT most agents will miss: NIRD is NOT free. The User Contribution Model (v2.2, valid from 1 Oct 2025) prices it at 'NIRD Data Lake 470 NOK per TB/year' and 'NIRD Data Peak 800 NOK per TB/year' for Category A, invoiced yearly to the institution. 20 TiB of Data Lake ≈ 9,400 NOK/yr. The bytes are unmetered but the TB-years are not. This fails the 'free' filter unless an EU-programme exemption applies ('Projects participating in EU programmes are exempted from contribution').

extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
